question.prompt: An inverted cone with base radius \(12\) cm and height \(18\) cm is full of water. The water is poured into a tall cylinder whose horizontal base has a radius of \(24\) cm. What is the height in centimeters of the water in the cylinder?

solutions.title: Equate the volumes
solutions.explanation:
The amount of water stays the same when it is poured, so we can equate its volumes in the two containers.

A cone of radius \(r\) and height \(H\) has volume \(\frac13\pi r^2H\). Thus the full cone contains
\[
V=\frac13\pi(12)^2(18)=864\pi
\]
cubic centimeters of water.

Let \(h\) be the water height in the cylinder, in centimeters. A cylinder's volume equals its base area times its height, so
\[
\pi(24)^2h=864\pi.
\]
Dividing by \(576\pi\) gives
\[
h=\frac{864}{576}=\boxed{1.5\text{ cm}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

solutions.title: Compare base areas
solutions.explanation:
An intermediate cylinder with radius \(12\) cm makes it easy to account separately for the cone's shape and the actual cylinder's wider base.

A cone holds one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height. Therefore, in a cylinder of radius \(12\) cm, this water would reach a height of
\[
18\div3=6\text{ cm}.
\]
The actual cylinder has radius \(24\) cm, twice as large. Since a circle's area is \(\pi r^2\), doubling the radius multiplies the base area by \(4\).

For the same water volume, base area times water height is constant. A base four times as large therefore gives one-fourth the height:
\[
h=6\div4=\boxed{1.5\text{ cm}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
